name: Monopod
body:
Monopods are short, dwarf-like humanoids notable for having only one leg and one massive foot.

Physical

Monopods are squat, dwarflike humanoids.

They are somewhat shorter than humans, but have wide builds. Monopods tend to have bronze or light brown skin, but lighter or darker shades have been observed. They wear their naturally curly hair in all manner of styles, just as humans do, although the men do tend to go bald by early adulthood.

The men traditionally wear short beards, but are not bound by this custom. Men and women alike dress in simple tunics and robes, and always go barefoot.

The monopods’ most striking feature is their single, wide leg, ending in a large, sturdy foot. Although they have only one foot, they are quite agile, and adept at using their broad lower appendage to keep their balance. Having only one leg does affect their speed, however, as their normal mode of locomotion is to make many short, plodding hops. However, they are capable of great bursts of speed when needed, as their single leg can suddenly recoil like a spring, launching them forward with surprising momentum.

Social

Monopods are often remembered for behavior that others find unusual, such as lying on their back and using their giant foot for shade or as an umbrella. However, the monopods themselves do not see their anatomy as anything unusual—neither a benefit nor an impairment, but simply a fact of life. It is perhaps this outlook that has made the monopods so accepting of others, whatever their appearance. Maimed and disfigured castoffs from other societies are readily accepted as members of monopod tribes, as are tieflings, fair folk, and others who have a hard time finding a home elsewhere due to their unusual appearance.

Monopods like to joke to strangers that they are divided into left-footers and right-footers, and that these factions have engaged in bitter dispute for centuries. In fact, there is no such division, and monopod feet come in all shapes and sizes. The concept of “right” or “left” in regards to feet is simply nonsense to them; the entire debate is an inside joke that merely displays the monopods’ dry sense of humor.

Monopod tribes tend to be closely tied to nature, many organizing into simple farming or fishing communities that dwell in unintrusive hillside burrows.

Alignment and Religion

Monopods are simple folk who enjoy a good laugh but rarely at others’ expense.

They tend toward Neutral or Neutral Good outlooks. A simple form of druidism is popular among them, as are gods of nature and community. As a people, they are welcoming of many different faiths.

Base Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You have excellent balance and perception, but your logic is sometimes lacking. Your ability score adjustments are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Int [standard].
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size.
Type You are a Humanoid with the monopod subtype.
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. However, you do not suffer any penalties to your Acrobatics check when jumping for having a movement rate of less than 30 feet.
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Dwarven, Giant, Gnome, and Goblin.
Alternate Traits
Foot Shield The sole of your massive foot is nearly as tough as steel. When you are prone, your foot provides you with a +2 shield bonus to your Armor Class. (As always, shield bonuses do not stack.)
Jump Kick When you make a charge attack by jumping at least 10 feet, you can end that charge with a slam attack that deals 2d4 damage + 1-1/2 times your Strength bonus. If you roll a natural 4 on at least one of the damage dice (including any bonus damage dice you roll on a critical hit), you can attempt a free bull rush maneuver against the target that does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
Jumper You are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump.
Low-Light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.
Skilled Monopods tend to be both outgoing and attuned to nature. You gain a +2 species bonus on Diplomacy and Knowledge (nature) checks.
Unusual Anatomy Because you have only one leg, you cannot wear magic items designed to be worn on two legs or two feet. However, your single leg imposes no penalties to Acrobatics checks or to your CMD against trip attempts.
Alternate Species Traits
Astonishing Balance You can move 10 feet instead of 5 feet when taking a crawl action. You also gain a +4 species bonus to your CMD against bull rush and trip combat maneuvers. This trait replaces jump kick.
Bold and Brash You gain a +2 bonus to Charisma instead of to Wisdom. This trait alters ability scores.
Trickster Your particularly strong sense of humor has made you good at playing pranks. You gain a +2 species bonus on Bluff and Perform (comedy) checks. This trait replaces skilled.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add a +1/3 bonus to your trap sense and to Acrobatics checks to jump.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Cleric Add a +1/2 bonus to Knowledge (nature) and Knowledge (religion) checks.
Druid Add +1/2 to your wild empathy bonus.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a dirty trick or trip attempt.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or trip attempt.
Oracle Add +1 spell known from the oracle spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level oracle spell you can cast.
